recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not re-remove AuditEvent or Provenance from the Patient compartment for this seed; FHIR-15906's specific defect is already resolved, and later FHIR-33155/FHIR-43373 decisions establish the current direct patient-link behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-15906 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for the Patient CompartmentDefinition. It reported that Provenance.target.subject and Provenance.target.patient were invalid/confusing chained parameters because Provenance.target can point to any resource, and the resolution asked to remove AuditEvent and Provenance from the compartment while adding notes about $everything and access control.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn history as b63ba456ef969b5e173fc94623f34884301e68cc, which changed AuditEvent from patient | agent.patient | entity.patient to patient and Provenance from target.subject | target.patient | patient to patient in source/compartments.xml. That removed the specific chained links that caused the reported search-framework ambiguity, though it did not literally remove the two resource rows.
additional_context: Later published/applied decisions supersede a literal removal reading. FHIR-33155 added explicit AuditEvent.patient and Provenance.patient elements and direct patient search parameters for deterministic patient-compartment discovery. FHIR-43373 then updated Patient $everything wording because Provenance and AuditEvent are now in the Patient compartment. The 2018 Zulip thread records the original chained-link concern, while the 2023 $everything thread records later acceptance that these resources are in the Patient compartment even if servers apply policy to returned resources.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/compartments.xml has no target.subject, target.patient, agent.patient, or entity.patient links and lists AuditEvent and Provenance only through direct patient. Current AuditEvent and Provenance source defines the corresponding direct .patient elements and patient search parameters, so removing these compartment entries now would conflict with later final decisions.
